units.title: 3.1 Factors affecting participation in physical activity and sport

outcomes.text: Study factors affecting participation in physical activity and sport.
Interpret data and graphs on body-system changes before, during and after exercise.
Explain how cardiovascular and respiratory changes meet exercise demands and how activity benefits them.
Explain the effect of activity on health (heart disease, blood pressure, cholesterol, stroke) and fitness (cardiac output).
Explain hormonal, neural and chemical control of the heart: anticipatory rise, blood redistribution, cardiac conduction, sympathetic and parasympathetic control.
Name the receptors that regulate responses: chemoreceptors, proprioceptors, baroreceptors.
Explain oxygen transport: haemoglobin, myoglobin, the oxyhaemoglobin dissociation curve and Bohr shift.
Explain venous return, its mechanisms and link to blood pressure.
Explain Starling's law of the heart.
Explain cardiovascular drift.
Explain arterio-venous oxygen difference and how it varies with exercise and training.
Explain lung volumes and their role in activity: residual, reserve, tidal, minute ventilation.
Explain gas exchange at alveoli and muscles, using diffusion and partial pressures.
Explain neural and chemical regulation of breathing during exercise.
Name the receptors that regulate breathing.
Explain how smoking harms the respiratory system and oxygen transport.
Compare slow twitch, fast glycolytic and fast oxidative glycolytic fibres for different sports.
Describe the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous system.
Explain the role of muscle spindles and Golgi tendon organs in PNF stretching.
Explain recruitment of muscle fibres: motor units, spatial and wave summation, all-or-none law, tetanus.
Describe joint actions in the sagittal plane: flexion, extension, hyperextension, plantar and dorsi flexion.
Describe joint actions in the frontal plane: adduction and abduction.
Describe horizontal abduction and adduction in the transverse plane.
Identify joint types, bones, agonists and antagonists, and isotonic and isometric contractions in sporting actions.
Explain aerobic energy transfer: glycolysis, Krebs cycle, beta oxidation, electron transport chain.
Explain anaerobic systems: ATP-PC and anaerobic glycolytic.
Explain the energy continuum for different intensities and durations, and ATP generation in fast and slow fibres.
Explain short, high-intensity energy transfer, including lactate threshold and OBLA.
Explain energy transfer in long, lower-intensity exercise and oxygen deficit.
Explain oxygen consumption in recovery (EPOC).
List factors affecting VO2 max.
Describe measuring energy expenditure: indirect calorimetry, lactate sampling, VO2 max test, RER.
Explain how altitude training, HIIT, plyometrics and SAQ affect energy systems.
Interpret graphs about skill acquisition theories.
Describe the characteristics of skill.
Place skills on continua: open-closed, discrete-serial-continuous, gross-fine, self-paced-externally paced, high-low, simple-complex, and justify the placement.
Explain positive, negative, zero and bilateral transfer and their effect on skill development.
Present practice as whole, progressive part or whole-part-whole.
Use massed, distributed, variable and mental practice.
Use skill classification to choose practice structure.
Describe the cognitive, associative and autonomous stages and how feedback differs.
Explain the learning plateau, its causes and solutions.
Explain insight learning, operant conditioning, observational learning and social development theory.
Explain how learning theories affect skill development.
Describe verbal, visual, manual and mechanical guidance.
Distinguish knowledge of performance from knowledge of results, positive from negative, intrinsic from extrinsic feedback.
Explain how feedback and guidance affect skill development.
Study memory models.
Explain input: senses, receptors, proprioception, perception, the DCR process, selective attention.
Explain decision making and short and long-term memory.
Describe the working memory model of Baddeley and Hitch.
Explain output and feedback.
Apply Whiting's information processing model to sport and its terms.
Define and relate reaction time, response time and movement time.
Explain Hick's law, psychological refractory period and the single channel hypothesis.
Define temporal and spatial anticipation and strategies to improve response time.
Explain Schmidt's schema theory: recall, recognition, initial conditions, response specifications, sensory consequences, outcomes.
Apply schema theory in sport.
Improve information processing through selective attention, chunking, chaining and schema.
Interpret data and graphs on participation in physical activity and sport.
Trace how sport was globalised, with football, tennis and athletics as the cases.
Describe pre-1780 society: two-tier class, rural, limited communication, illiteracy, harsh life.
Describe sporting recreation then: mob football and real tennis.
Explain how the Industrial Revolution, urbanisation, transport, Empire and factories shaped sport 1780-1900.
Explain the roles of churches, local authorities, public schools and universities.
Explain the three-tier class system and growth of governing bodies.
Explain the changing role of women and amateur versus professional status.
Explain the development of association football, lawn tennis, athletics events and the Wenlock Olympian Games.
Explain the Golden Triangle of commercialisation, media and sport.
Explain the changing status of amateurs and professionals since 1950.
Explain factors in the emergence of elite female performers in football, tennis and athletics.
Study the impact of sport on society and society on sport.
Define society, socialisation, social control, social change, inequality and social structures.
Explain social action theory applied to sport.
Identify underrepresented groups: disability, ethnicity, gender, disadvantaged.
Define discrimination, stereotyping and prejudice.
Explain barriers to participation and solutions for underrepresented groups.
Explain health, fitness and social benefits of raising participation.
Explain how Sport England and partners raise grass-roots participation.

units.title: 3.2 Factors affecting optimal performance in physical activity and sport

outcomes.text: Study factors affecting optimal performance.
Explain adaptations of body systems to training and lifestyle.
Explain the exercise function of carbohydrate, fibre, fat, protein, vitamins, minerals and water.
Explain effects of supplements and dietary manipulation: creatine, sodium bicarbonate, caffeine, glycogen loading.
Define quantitative, qualitative, objective, subjective, validity and reliability.
Explain warm-up and cool-down effects and static and ballistic stretching.
Apply specificity, overload, reversibility, recovery and FITT.
Apply periodisation: macro, meso, micro cycles, preparation, competition, transition, tapering, peaking.
Match training methods to fitness: HIIT, continuous, fartlek, circuit, weights, PNF.
Distinguish acute from chronic injuries with examples.
Describe injury prevention: screening, protective equipment, warm-up, flexibility, taping, bracing.
Describe rehabilitation and recovery methods and their physiological reasons.
Explain the importance of sleep and nutrition for recovery.
Use biomechanical definitions, equations and units, and plot and interpret biomechanical graphs.
Apply Newton's three laws of linear motion to sport.
Define scalars with equations and units: speed and distance.
Explain centre of mass and the factors affecting stability.
Describe the three classes of lever and their use in the body.
Explain mechanical advantage and disadvantage of each lever class.
Identify forces on a performer in linear motion: gravity, friction, air resistance, muscular force, weight.
Define vectors with equations and units: velocity, displacement, acceleration, momentum.
Define scalars: mass, speed and distance.
Explain impulse and momentum in sprinting using force-time graphs.
Apply Newton's laws to angular motion.
Define angular displacement, velocity and acceleration with units.
Explain conservation of angular momentum, moment of inertia and angular velocity.
Explain factors affecting horizontal displacement of projectiles.
Explain factors affecting flight paths, such as shot put and shuttle.
Explain vector components of parabolic flight.
Explain dynamic fluid force: drag and lift.
Explain factors that change drag in sport.
Apply the Bernoulli principle to upward lift (discus) and downward force (cyclists, racing cars).
Interpret graphs about sport psychology theories.
Study psychological factors that influence an individual.
Debate nature versus nurture in personality (trait, social learning).
Explain the interactionist perspective and how it improves performance.
Explain the triadic model of attitudes and their formation.
Explain changing attitudes by cognitive dissonance and persuasive communication.
Explain drive theory, inverted U, catastrophe and zone of optimal functioning theories.
Apply arousal theories in practice and describe peak flow.
Distinguish somatic, cognitive, trait and state anxiety.
Compare observation, questionnaires and physiological measures of anxiety.
Distinguish aggression from assertive behaviour.
Explain instinct, frustration-aggression, social learning and aggressive cue theories.
Describe strategies to control aggression.
Distinguish intrinsic, extrinsic, tangible and intangible motivation.
Explain Atkinson's model of achievement motivation, Nach and Naf.
Explain situational factors: incentive value and probability of success.
Explain achievement goal theory: outcome and task orientation.
Describe strategies to develop approach behaviours.
Explain social facilitation and inhibition using Zajonc's model and evaluation apprehension.
Describe strategies to remove adverse social facilitation effects.
Explain group formation using Tuckman's model.
Explain task and social cohesion.
Explain Steiner's model, faulty group processes, the Ringelmann effect and social loafing.
Describe strategies to improve cohesion, productivity and overcome social loafing.
Distinguish outcome, performance and process goals and their benefits.
Apply SMARTER goal setting.
Explain the attribution process and Weiner's model in sport.
Link attribution to task persistence and motivation.
Explain self-serving bias and attribution retraining.
Explain learned helplessness and strategies to avoid it.
Distinguish self-efficacy, self-confidence and self-esteem.
Explain Bandura's model of self-efficacy and its four sources.
Explain Vealey's model of self-confidence.
Explain home field advantage.
Describe strategies to build self-efficacy.
Describe characteristics of effective leaders.
Compare autocratic, democratic and laissez-faire styles and when each suits.
Distinguish prescribed from emergent leaders.
Explain Fiedler's contingency theory and Chelladurai's multi-dimensional model.
Define stress and stressor and use warm-up for stress management.
Explain cognitive techniques: mental rehearsal, visualisation, imagery, attentional control, thought stopping, self-talk.
Explain somatic techniques: biofeedback, centering, breathing control, progressive muscle relaxation.

topics.title: 3.2.4 Sport and society and the role of technology

subtopics.title: Concepts of sport and elite development

outcomes.text: Study sport and society and technology in sport.
Describe physical recreation, sport, physical education and school sport on the sporting continuum.
Compare these concepts.
Identify factors needed from talent identification to elite performance.
Explain the roles of National Governing Bodies, National Institutes of Sport and UK Sport.
Describe support services for talent development.
Describe UK Sport's World Class Performance Programme, Gold Event Series and talent programmes.
Define amateurism, the Olympic Oath, sportsmanship, gamesmanship and win ethic.
Explain positive and negative deviance.
Explain causes and implications of violence by performers, spectators and in sport.
Describe strategies to prevent violence.
Explain why elite performers use illegal drugs.
Explain physiological effects of EPO, anabolic steroids and beta blockers.
Explain positive and negative implications of drug taking for sport and performer.
Describe strategies to eliminate performance-enhancing drugs.
Argue for and against drug taking and testing.
Explain sports legislation for performers, officials, coaches and spectators.
Explain positive and negative effects of commercialisation, sponsorship and media on performer, coach, official, audience and sport.
Describe technology for data collection: video analysis, metabolic cart, GPS, motion tracking.
Explain data quality: validity, reliability and integrity.
Describe uses of analytics: fitness, technique, injury prevention, game analysis, talent ID.
Explain how equipment and facility technology affects participation and performance.
Evaluate positive and negative impacts of technology on sport, performer, coach and audience.
